query: How much does the Lumen Arc cost, and when will it ship?
answer: The Lumen Arc costs $899 and ships on March 15, 2026. Beyond pricing, the glasses weigh 48 grams, use micro-LED projectors rated for outdoor visibility, and last a full day of typical glanceable use on a single charge. They run ArcOS and pair with both Android and iOS phones.

knowledge_sources.content: Lumen Devices today unveiled the Lumen Arc, its first pair of augmented-reality glasses, at the company's annual developer conference in Austin. The Arc projects a translucent heads-up display onto each lens, letting wearers see notifications, walking directions, and live translations without reaching for a phone. The company called the launch the result of a four-year hardware effort and its most ambitious product to date.

The Arc weighs 48 grams, about the same as a regular pair of sunglasses, and uses a pair of micro-LED projectors rated at 1,000 nits for outdoor visibility. Onboard sensors include a 12-megapixel camera, dual microphones, and an inertial measurement unit for head tracking. Lumen says the frames will come in three sizes and two colors, charcoal and sand.

Battery life is a central question for any wearable. Lumen claims the Arc runs for a full day of typical glanceable use on a single charge, with a companion carrying case providing two additional recharges. The glasses run ArcOS, a stripped-down platform that pairs with both Android and iOS phones, and Lumen has opened a software development kit so outside developers can build their own overlays.

Lumen said the Arc would be available in select markets later this year, beginning with the United States and Germany, with enterprise customers getting early access through a partner program. Executives repeatedly declined to discuss pricing during the event, saying only that the company would share more on cost and timing closer to launch. Pre-orders are not yet open.

We didn't want to build a screen you wear on your face, we wanted something you'd forget you had on, said Lumen chief executive Dana Okafor during the keynote. Okafor said the team deliberately left out a built-in speaker to keep the frames light, relying instead on bone-conduction audio routed through the temples.
